**1. A 401(k) RMD was counted inside an IRA withdrawal (5 households).** Each owner turned 73 in 2025 (factor 26.5). Each signed a form taking the RMDs of "all three retirement accounts added together" as one payment from an IRA. IRA RMDs can be combined across IRAs, but a 401(k) RMD has to come out of the 401(k) itself. The CRM says all five had retired, so the still-working exception doesn't apply. The IRA RMDs were met; nothing came out of any of the five 401(k)s. Each payment equals the three per-account RMDs added up to the cent, so the missing amount is exactly the 401(k)'s own RMD.

- **HH-5271, Teodoro Villanueva:** 401(k) SYN-52710004, **$12,729.96**. The CRM gives no amount, but the $44,202.50 IRA payment equals all three accounts' RMDs combined.

**2. Inherited IRAs with no 2025 distribution (5 households).** In each case the prior custodian confirms the original owner had already started RMDs before dying. That means the child who inherited must take yearly RMDs within the 10-year window. The IRS waived penalties for 2021–2024, so 2025 is the first year that counts. None of these accounts shows any 2025 distribution, only sales and buys within the account. Each RMD is the 2024 year-end balance divided by the heir's own life expectancy, reduced by one for each year since the first required year.

- **HH-0842, Ines Trevelyan:** SYN-08420002, **$7,090.19** (factor 45.7). The original owner died in 2024, so 2025 is the first required year.

**What checked out:**
- Five owners took their 401(k) and IRA RMDs separately and in full: HH-0989, HH-0637, HH-0555, HH-0410 and HH-5814.
- Ten single-IRA owners had their QCD plus distribution equal their computed RMD exactly: HH-0222, 0885, 0168, 0445, 6047, 6590, 0190, 0414, 0782 and 0642.
- Five inherited IRAs had no 2025 requirement, because the original owner died before RMDs began: HH-0571, 0716, 0328, 0330 and 7683.
- None of the 2025 deaths left an RMD-age IRA owner behind.

**Uncertainties:**
- Balances are 2024 year-end positions plus cash, which I added up myself. The method reproduces every payment the custodian made, so I trust it.
- The life-expectancy factors come from the IRS tables, recalled from memory. They are not in these files.
- The inherited-IRA cases depend on reading these heirs as owners of an IRA. If the question was meant only for owners' own accounts, the answer is the five 401(k) cases.
- HH-0642's owner turned 73 in 2024. I didn't check whether her 2024 RMD (due by 1 April 2025) was taken, since that's outside the 2025 question.

You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds the records of every client household of the firm as they stood on 15 April 2026, one folder per household under households/<household ID>/, each with the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/) and its CRM (crm/).

The advisor asks: which IRA owners in the book had a 2025 required minimum distribution, from any of their retirement accounts, that was not met?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "found" if one or more owners did, "none_found" if none did, or "unresolved" if the files settle no household as found and leave some unresolved
- "households": one entry per household with such an owner, each as {"household_id": ..., "owner_id": the owner's person ID, "account_ids": the accounts the unmet distribution had to come from, "shortfall": the amount not taken, "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "unresolved": the households the files cannot settle, each as {"household_id": ..., "explanation": one sentence}, or [] if none
- "figures": every figure you relied on from the files, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed from them rather than read
- "explanation": two or three sentences
